title: Notes in a scale
learned: A quantizer moves any voltage to the nearest note of a scale
SCALE picks the notes allowed, ROOT the key
Put the quantizer between a CV source and V/OCT: any knob position is now in tune

steps.why: The melody from the last lesson plays, a bit out of tune: its step voltages fall between notes. A quantizer snaps any voltage to the nearest note of a scale you choose.
steps.do: The quantizer (JX-QNT) is next to the sequencer. Press Next.

steps.why: The quantizer goes between the sequencer's CV and the oscillator's pitch.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from CV of the sequencer to the V/OCT input of the quantizer (on its left; CV already has a cable). Then drag a cable from the V/OCT output of the quantizer (on its right) to V/OCT of the oscillator. The second cable replaces the old one there.
steps.after: The same melody, now in tune: every step lands on a note of C major, the quantizer's starting scale.

steps.why: The scale decides the mood: which notes are allowed.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn SCALE of the quantizer. Its NOTES display shows which notes the scale uses.
steps.after: Major sounds bright, minor darker, pentatonic can never sound wrong, chromatic allows all twelve notes (and quantizes only to the nearest semitone).

steps.why: ROOT moves the whole scale to another key.
steps.after: The melody moved to a new key and kept its shape. To play along with other music, set ROOT and SCALE to its key.

steps.why: Now the sequencer knobs are safe to play with.
steps.do: Turn a few step knobs of the sequencer, in small moves.
steps.after: Every position is a note of the scale: you can compose by ear without knowing which voltage is which note.
steps.try: Turn OCTAVE of the quantizer: the whole melody jumps an octave up or down.

steps.do: Any voltage, quantized, becomes a melody in key. Press Next to finish.
